messages:
Emma: Hey — hitting a weird Next.js app-router issue when using the JS SDK in a server component. Root cause looks like a server-only module (node:fs) in one of our helper libs causing the bundler to emit CJS and then runtime fails in edge/experimental ESM. Repro: https://github.com/redwood-internal/next-dx-repro (branch: cjs-esm-hydrate).

Jason: can you paste the error?

Emma: error: 'Hydration failed because the initial UI does not match...' + stack shows require(...) is not a function. Happens when dynamic import + interop wrapper used. Minimal repro uses:
```js
// server-component.jsx
const sdk = await import('redwood-sdk');
const client = sdk.default ?? sdk;
```
Works in Node server, fails in edge/runtime.

Priya: :thinking: This smells like default export interop between CJS and ESM. TS types also export as `export =` in v1 which doesn't map to `default`. Are we shipping both flavors?

Alex: We hit similar in prod. Next's bundler sometimes rewrites imports causing `module.exports =` to be treated as a namespace. Quick hack: `const client = (await import('redwood-sdk')).default?.client ?? (await import('redwood-sdk')).client` but ugly and double-importy.

Jason: Could we add an ESM build that uses `export default` and a tiny compat CJS entry that does `module.exports = require('./esm').default`? That usually smooths over runtime interop.

Priya: For typing, if we provide `declare module 'redwood-sdk' { export default typeof Client }` in an index.d.ts and ship it in "types", TS inference in ESM contexts improves. Also ensure package.json has a proper "exports" map for both ./ and ./cjs.

Emma: I tried next.config.js tweak:
```js
module.exports = {
  experimental: { esmExternals: 'loose' }
}
```
That made bundler keep ESM but caused other deps to break. Not a general fix.

Alex: Are we sure this is specific to server/client boundary? Could a client import leak into a server bundle? If you import a server-only module in module scope, Next will error. Try moving node:fs usage inside an async function.

Emma: Good point — I moved fs usage into a utils function that's only invoked on server and that fixed one variant. But the interop hydration error persists.

Priya: Action items: (1) Add a tiny ESM-first CI test against a Next app-router edge sample. (2) Add an examples/nextjs-app-router-esm-cjs sample to the repo with recommended patterns. (3) Update package.json exports + types and ship an ESM-first bundle. I'll open a PR for the d.ts augmentation. Assigning to myself.

CI Bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-internal/sdk/pull/789 — unit tests failing on node 16. :construction:

Emma: Thanks — I'll drop the repro link and screenshots into the PR. Also we should add a docs note: 'If you see "require is not a function" in Next edge, prefer the ESM interop pattern and avoid static requires at module scope.'

Jason: +1. Also let's add the recommended dynamic import snippet in docs:
```js
const mod = await import('redwood-sdk');
const sdk = mod?.default ?? mod;
```

Priya: And include an app-router-aware example showing server-only module placement (inside route handler or server action) and how to avoid static requires.

Emma: Cool, will do. Thanks all :rocket:
